_comment: Guided tour for the k2 distribution calculator. Steps point at the real controls and wait for the user to press them. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What this tool is for
steps.text:
Every FRET distance you report assumes an orientation factor κ², almost always 2/3. This tool asks how much that assumption could be costing you.

It does not measure κ² — nothing can. It turns anisotropies you can measure into the range of κ² consistent with them, and from that into a range of distances.

Six steps. You press the buttons; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Start with the worst case
steps.text:
Pick Isotropic first. It means the dipoles are randomly oriented and completely frozen — no reorientation at all during the donor lifetime.

It is not a model of a real sample. It is the reference to compare against, and it needs no anisotropy inputs.

steps.title: Compute, and read the mean
steps.text:
Press Compute. The mean κ² comes back at 2/3 — exactly the value everyone assumes.

Now look at the plot. The distribution is broad and piles up near zero. A correct mean is not a safe assumption: it is the spread that moves distances, and this is the shape that does the damage.

await.hint: Press Compute and look at SD κ² and the plot.

steps.title: Now use your own dyes
steps.text:
Switch to WIC (Cone). Each dye now reorients freely inside a cone whose half-angle comes from its residual anisotropy — the realistic picture for a dye on a flexible linker.

This is the model you will use on real data.

steps.title: The inputs are anisotropy fits, not guesses
steps.text:
r₀ is the fundamental anisotropy of your dye. r_D∞ and r_A∞ are the residual anisotropies of the donor and of the directly excited acceptor — both come from ordinary time-resolved anisotropy fits.

Try raising r_D∞ toward r₀ and recomputing: a more restricted donor widens the κ² range, and with it the distance range. That is the whole point of the tool.

await.hint: Change r_D∞, press Compute, and watch SD R_app/R_DA.

steps.title: The number to quote
steps.text:
SD R_app/R_DA is the answer — the relative systematic uncertainty κ² puts on your distance. Under about 0.10 is the usual result for long flexible linkers, and it is why 2/3 has survived as a convention.

The fourth input, r_AD∞ (the FRET-sensitized acceptor), tightens the bound further by fixing the angle δ between the dyes — but only tick r_AD known if you actually measured it. Without it, the wider bound is the honest one.

Press ? for the models and the theory.
